claims.text: JPMorgan paid USVI $75m (Sept 2023): $30m charities, $25m anti-trafficking law enforcement, $20m legal fees; no admission; USVI had sought at least $190m incl. a $150m civil penalty; alleged JPM kept him as a 'valued client' after 2006 arrest and 2008 plea; JPM 'deeply regrets any association'; Staley settled with JPM confidentially.
Estate paid USVI more than $105m (Dec 2022) plus half the proceeds of selling both islands; executors deny wrongdoing.

claims.text: NYDFS consent order, $150m (July 2020): Deutsche Bank onboarded Epstein 2013; failed to monitor despite public criminal record; hundreds of transactions totalling millions; payments to Russian models, women's tuition, hotel and rent, women with Eastern European surnames, alleged co-conspirators; over $7m settlements and over $6m to law firms; more than $800,000 suspicious cash withdrawals over about four years; Sewing: onboarding 'a critical mistake'.
JPMorgan filed suspicious activity reports on over $1bn of Epstein-linked transactions weeks after his death in 2019 (NYT).

UK tribunal (26 June 2025) upheld the FCA's 2023 ban on Jes Staley; fine cut from £1.8m to about £1.1m; FCA found Barclays' 2019 letter misleading and Staley reckless; contact via his daughter until at least Feb 2017; Barclays withheld £17.8m in awards.

claims.text: Dimon deposition (26 May 2023): Mary Erdoes (private banking) and Jes Staley could have decided to retain Epstein; general counsel Stephen Cutler was the 'ultimate decider'; Cutler's July 2011 emails said Epstein 'should not be a client'; Dimon said he had no involvement and first learned of Epstein in 2019; Erdoes went to the townhouse to end the relationship in 2013.
Pension-fund derivative suit against JPMorgan's directors dismissed by Judge Rakoff, Aug 2023, for failure to make pre-suit demand on the board.

NYDFS consent order (2020): a relationship manager who had worked with Epstein proposed him in 2013; head of wealth management said the Americas AML head and Americas general counsel agreed he could skip the Reputational Risk Committee; that email was relied on to open other accounts; Feb 2015 committee decided 'business as usual' with conditions; 120 wires totalling $2.65M to Butterfly Trust beneficiaries or suspected prostitutes.

NYT via Fox Business (Jul 2020): relationship manager was Paul Morris, formerly on Epstein's JPMorgan account; approval by Charles Packard, head of US wealth management; both visited Epstein in Jan 2015.

ThinkAdvisor (28 May 2026): Morris worked on Epstein's JPMorgan account from about 2009, joined Deutsche late 2012 and moved the account in Sept 2013, joined Bank of America's Merrill in 2016; kept contacting Epstein until July 2019; gifts to Epstein and Lesley Groff; not accused of a crime, not a defendant; deposed 2023.

Doe v. Bank of America (S.D.N.Y. 25-cv-08520) alleged Leon Black used BofA accounts to send $170M to Epstein, and that Maxwell used BofA accounts; Black not a defendant, denies wrongdoing; settlement let Black avoid a deposition set for 26 Mar 2026.

entries.topic: The wider banking web and Black's other payments

claims.text: Reuters (via TribLive): a JPMorgan SAR filed with FinCEN soon after Epstein's death, unsealed in USVI v. JPMorgan after NYT/WSJ requests, listed one Goldman Sachs account and three accounts at HSBC's Swiss private bank; flagged transfers, no amounts; Goldman: relationship ended, assets transferred out in 2010; HSBC declined comment.

WSJ (via iTiger): Wells Fargo held Epstein or Epstein-related accounts in his later years; TD Bank closed accounts of his lawyer and accountant in 2019; FirstBank Puerto Rico called him a legacy relationship inherited when it bought Chase's USVI operations in 2002; Honeycomb Partners received at least $60M 2016-19 incl. $20M March 2019 (says no relationship); Boothbay ~$38M 2014-17, forced redemption after arrest; an Epstein entity invested in Tudor Futures Fund 2001-14, $13.5M received (Tudor: Jones did not know him); Valar >$20M; Blockchain Capital bought $15M of shares.

NYT via Boston Globe (25 Mar 2026): Black paid ~$20M to a dozen women; Oct 2015 agreement: $10M to Southern Trust plus $10M donation to Gratitude America, reportedly funded through BV70 LLC (Black's yacht company); Epstein appears to have helped set up payments to Guzel Ganieva ($18M over 15 years, NDA, Oct 2015) through a generically named trust; Black says payments to Epstein were for tax and estate work.
